p: Here's the thing about a farm park: the best bits are rarely the ones you planned. A goat decides your coat zip is lunch, a hen wanders across the path like she owns the place, and suddenly the kids are giggling so hard they forget they ever wanted the tablet. The Meadows Farm Village is that sort of easy, unfussy day out, and it works best when you let the little ones set the pace rather than marching them round a checklist.

A few tips make it go smoothly. Bring hand wipes and a bottle of water for after the animal-stroking, because there won't always be a sink right where you need one. Pack a spare pair of socks in the car (trust us on this one after a wet week), and if you've got a toddler, a sling or a sturdy buggy copes with farm paths far better than a flimsy stroller. Small details on the day can change, so a quick look at the farm's own updates before setting off saves any disappointment.

Caerphilly itself gives you plenty to chew on afterwards, quite literally. The town lent its name to Caerphilly cheese, the crumbly, mild one that's been a lunchbox favourite for generations, and the summer Big Cheese festival turns the streets round the castle into a riot of food stalls, music and medieval-style fun. If you're still hungry for history, Castell Coch, the fairytale red castle peeping out of the woods at Tongwynlais, is a short drive away, and Cardiff is close enough for a seaside-meets-city evening down Cardiff Bay. Not bad for a day that started with a goat chewing your zip.
